candidates.sourceReviewStatus: count-level pass and approved representative source; motion use only
candidates.positivePrompt: Scientific educational image-to-video using the attached approved still as the exact identity, anatomy, framing, lighting, palette, and background reference. Exactly one complete full-body Tyrannosaurus rex with a deep skull that is very broad posteriorly and narrows toward the snout, low rounded postorbital bosses, small polygonal scales, exactly two extremely small chest-held forelimbs with exactly two fingers on each readable hand, exactly two strong grounded hind limbs, and one complete continuous tail. Perform one clearly readable but restrained, child-safe open-mouth vocal display over five seconds. During the first third, rotate only the lower jaw smoothly downward at the natural jaw hinge to a moderate twelve-to-eighteen-degree gape. Keep the upper skull, snout length, eye, nostril, head height, and short muscular neck stable. Natural irregularly sized teeth remain firmly attached to their original upper and lower jaw edges without changing count, spacing, shape, or position. Briefly reveal one low tongue and a clean shadowed pink-brown mouth interior. During the middle third, hold the moderate gape while the throat and upper chest expand once very slightly as if exhaling. Do not turn the head, lunge, walk, or move the arms. During the final third, close the lower jaw smoothly until the lips cover the teeth again, then settle into the exact source pose. Both feet, every toe, both tiny arms, torso, pelvis, and tail remain at the source coordinates. Fixed camera, fixed crop, fixed forest, wet ground, vegetation, shadows, lighting, and exposure. This is a silent, non-graphic generated behavior hypothesis suitable for children ages five to fourteen.

Tyrannosaurus keeps one deep broad skull, two tiny two-fingered arms, two grounded hind limbs, and one complete heavy tail. Triceratops lowers the rigid skull and frill six to eight degrees and braces without stepping. Both animals remain on their original banks, never overlap or touch, then settle. Fixed camera, fixed crop, stable trees, water, ground, shadows, color, and exposure; crisp readable anatomy in every frame. This non-graphic attack attempt is a generated ecological hypothesis, not direct behavioral evidence.
